content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic:
Operator-installed correlation rule (CortexSim never writes it to the tenant). Alert name EXACTLY as this rule's name; severity Medium (only Medium or higher opens or joins a case); Scheduled, every 10 minutes, query time frame 1 hour; Issue Suppression enabled, Duration time 1 hour, Fields agent_id; alert field mapping: agent_hostname -> Host Name, agent_id -> Agent ID (the mapped artifacts are what let a correlation issue join a case); NO MITRE tag (an issue tagged T1036 would also be credited to the validation rows of SIM-EDR-026 step 1 and step 2, because every row of a step shares the step's technique). TESTED AS A QUERY, NOT AS A RULE. On 2026-11-14 at 01:11 UTC the XQL below, the not in lists and the !~= regex included, was run in the lab tenant as an ordinary read-only query over a one-hour time frame, and the tenant accepted it. It returned one row for pov-target-01: legs 3, events 30, first_seen 00:50:55.117, last_seen 00:52:55.267 (SIM-EDR-026 run 7714f4ce, 00:50:47 to 00:52:57). The rule has not been installed (no tenant write was made), so it has not run on a schedule and has raised no issue. Its alter, comp, then filter shape follows CR-EDR-0023, which was tested read-only in the lab tenant on 2026-11-11. It is built only from process and file events SIM-EDR-026 produces on one host. No leg names the sandbox, so the rule matches the same behaviour at any path other than the four system paths it excludes: /usr/sbin/crond, /sbin/crond, /usr/bin/crond and /bin/crond. On a host whose packaged daemon lives anywhere else, ordinary cron activity gives the launched and spawned legs, so add that path to the three exclusion lists before enabling the rule tenant-wide. Three legs: planted (a file named crond is created, written or renamed outside the system paths, or cp or mv is started with a destination that ends in /crond and is not one of them), launched (a process whose image name is crond starts from outside the system paths) and spawned (a process is started by such a crond). It fires for one agent that shows at least two of the three, so one missing file sub-type does not silence it; SIM-EDR-026 produces all three. Repeats: the rule matches again on every scheduled run while the events stay inside the one-hour time frame. With the suppression above only the first match per agent_id raises an issue in that hour, so one run of SIM-EDR-026 gives one issue; that is the behaviour the product documentation describes for issue suppression and it has not been exercised in the lab. With suppression left off (the product default) one run gives up to six issues. There is no current_time in the rule: the time frame bounds it. XQL:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| alter leg = if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name = "crond" and action_process_image_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"), "launched", if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and actor_process_image_name = "crond" and actor_process_image_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"), "spawned", if(event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START and action_process_image_name in ("cp", "mv") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "/crond[ ]*$" and action_process_image_command_line !~= "[ ](/usr)?/s?bin/crond[ ]*$", "planted", if(event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE, ENUM.FILE_RENAME) and action_file_name = "crond" and action_file_path not in ("/usr/sbin/crond", "/sbin/crond", "/usr/bin/crond", "/bin/crond"), "planted", "other"))))
| filter leg in ("planted", "launched", "spawned")
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, count() as events, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 2
rules.name: EDR-026 Crond Lookalike Planted And Launched
